newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FPHC to float two bln pesos debt papers.
newsitem.headline: FPHC to float two bln pesos debt papers.

text.p: First Philippine Holdings Corp said on Wednesday it planned to float 2.0 billion pesos worth of long-term commercial paper to raise funds for the expansion of its energy, real estate and infrastructure businesses.
The firm said in a statement it had asked approval from the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to issue the debt papers, with PCI Capital Corp as issue manager and underwriter.

Proceeds from the offering would be used to finance its investments in First Gas Holdings Corp, Panay Power and Panay Electric, Rockwell Land Corp, First Philippine Realty and Development Corp, and First Philippine Infrastructure Development Corp, it said.
First Gas, a joint venture between FPHC and British Gas Plc, plans to construct a 990-megawatt power plant in Batangas near Manila.

Rockwell Land, a partnership between FPHC, Benpres Holdings Corp and the Manila Electric Co, plans to develop a residential and commercial centre on a 15.5-hectare property in Manila's Makati business district.
First Philippine Realty, a unit of FPHC, also plans to develop a 300-hectare industrial estate south of Manila.
FPHC also has an equity in First Philippine Infrastructure, the firm that plans to rehabilitate and expand the expressways in Philippines' main Luzon island.
The firm did not give further details of the issue.
